title: logkit normalized log record
description: One log event in its normalized form: the cross-language wire record every logkit implementation emits and every consumer reads. This schema is the source of truth for the record's field names, types and required-vs-optional status; logkit-logging.spec.md is the normative standard around it (level semantics, timestamp derivation, canonical serialization, dual machine+human rendering, normalization of native library output) and logkit.contract.json carries the normalization data those rules key on. The root object is CLOSED: `fields` is the only extension point, so a consumer can validate strictly without a later addition breaking it. Nothing here is a rendering: a record is data, and both the one-line JSON and the human line are renderings of the same record.

schema_version.description: MAJOR version of this record contract. A consumer built against version N refuses a record declaring more than N rather than reading unknown semantics; the top-level field set is frozen for the life of a MAJOR, so a consumer built against N reads every N record.

timestamp.description: When the event happened, from the emitter's wall clock. Always UTC, always exactly three fractional digits.

level.description: Severity of the event. Closed set; see $defs/severity for the ordinal each name carries.

service.description: Logical emitter the record belongs to - the CLI, daemon or job name, fixed at logger construction. Identifies WHO logged; a sub-component within it belongs in `fields`.

message.description: What happened, as a short constant phrase. Variable data belongs in `fields`, never interpolated here - an interpolated message cannot be grouped or counted across events. Single line: control characters, including newline, are excluded so both renderings stay one line.

service_version.description: Version of the emitting build, when it knows one. Free-form (a semver, a git describe, a build id) because not every build has a released version. Absent, never null, when unknown.

fields.description: Structured context for this event: the variable data that would otherwise be interpolated into `message`. The ONLY extension point of the record - a key not defined here is legal, a new top-level record field is not. Omitted entirely when empty; never emitted as {} or null.

propertyNames.description: A key may not collide with a root field name: consumers that flatten a record into one namespace would silently shadow the root field. Authored keys are snake_case by convention; keys carried in verbatim from a foreign producer keep their original spelling, since any case transformation would be ambiguous and therefore non-deterministic.

native_level.description: RESERVED, set only by the normalization pass: the source's own level token, preserved when it mapped to a canonical level that is not its equivalent (`trace` -> `debug`, `panic` -> `fatal`). Absent for a pure alias and for anything logkit emitted itself.

error.description: The failure that caused this event, when one did. Independent of `level`: an error-level record need not carry it, and a warn-level record may - never infer one from the other. This is logkit's log-side view of a failure and is NOT clikit's Error contract; how a clikit error maps onto these keys is fixed by the clikit contract, not here.

message.description: The failure's own message, verbatim from the error value. Single line: when the error's text spans lines, its first line is carried here and the full text belongs in `fields` under a key the caller chooses.

kind.description: The error's type as the emitting language names it (Go concrete type, Rust type path, Python exception class). Absent when the language cannot name one.

stack.description: Stack frames, outermost-call first, one frame per element. Omitted when no stack was captured; never an empty array.

caller.description: Source location of the log call. Optional because capturing it costs a stack walk; when captured it is always complete enough to open the file.

file.description: Path from the module root, never absolute - an absolute path embeds the build machine's directory layout, which differs per builder and breaks byte-identity across languages and hosts.

line.description: 1-based line number of the log call.

function.description: Enclosing function or method as the language names it. Absent when the runtime cannot resolve one.

root_field_name.description: Every root field name, in one place: the root `properties` keys are exactly this set, and `fields` keys are checked against it so a context key can never shadow a record field.

level.description: The closed level set. Exactly five members, lowercase, no aliases and no `trace`/`panic`/`off` - a level outside this set is a normalization failure, never a default. Adding or removing a member is a MAJOR change, because downstream matches on it are exhaustive.

severity.description: Normative severity ordinal per level, carried beside the enum it keys so the two cannot drift. Not a record field and never serialized: it exists so every implementation compares levels identically (a record is emitted when severity(level) >= severity(threshold)) and so a foreign scale can be mapped onto this one by number. Ordinals are spaced by ten to leave room for a future MAJOR to interleave a level without renumbering.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339 date-time in UTC with the `Z` offset and exactly three fractional digits (milliseconds), always present even when zero. Fixed width (24 characters), so records sort lexicographically in the same order they sort chronologically. A finer clock reading is TRUNCATED toward zero, never rounded: rounding can order an event after one that happened later.

line.description: A non-empty single-line string: no control characters, so it survives both the one-line JSON rendering and the human rendering unchanged.
